string.text: In the mid-13th century, Kraków and Sandomierz were ruled by Duke Bolesław V the Chaste of the Piast dynasty, whose lands formed the political heart of Lesser Poland. The duchy was drawn into struggles among the rival Piast princes and maintained close ties with Hungary, while its eastern territories faced threats from Ruthenian forces, Lithuanians, and the Mongols, whose devastating invasion of 1259–1260 struck both Sandomierz and Kraków.

In 1259 the Principality of Smolensk is ruled by Prince Gleb Rostislavich of the Rostislavichi, a Rurikid house that has held the upper Dnieper since the twelfth century. The city escaped the worst of the Mongol sack that broke Kiev and Vladimir, but after 1249 it sits in the shadow of the Vladimir grand princes and, from the 1270s, of Horde census and tribute. Junior brothers hold the appanages of Mstislavl and the eastern grods around Vyazma, while Lithuania presses from the west and Toropets and Polotsk watch the same river roads.

In 1259 the Principality of Kyiv is the ruined southern table held in name by Alexander Yaroslavich, Grand Prince of Vladimir, who received Kiev from the Horde in 1249 and never made it his residence. Viceroys and local houses keep the Dnieper grods, the Porosie Black-Hat frontier at Korsun and Kotelnica, and the remnant Bolokhov seat at Mezhibozhye after Daniel of Galicia burned that land in 1256-57. The city pays Horde tribute; Lithuania and the Galician-Volhynian princes press from the west.

In 1259 the Kingdom of Ruthenia (Regnum Russiae) is the Galician-Volhynian realm of King Daniel Romanovich, crowned at Drohychyn in 1253. After the Mongols razed Halych he sits at Kholm. His brother Vasilko holds Volodymyr; his sons Lev, Roman, Mstislav, and Shvarn hold Belz, Lutsk, Chertoryisk, and the royal household. A marriage alliance with Mindaugas of Lithuania stands, but Burundai's 1259 ultimatum has forced the brothers to pull down their walls. The Horde is overlord; Poland and Kyiv watch the same frontier.
